cortina.title: Cortina d'Ampezzo
cortina.subtitle: Legendary Dolomite playground, with epic ski terrain and towering pinnacles
cortina.description:
Cortina d'Ampezzo sits beneath dramatic limestone walls in the heart of the UNESCO World Heritage Dolomites, and hosts mountain activities year-round. Stage of the 1956 Winter Olympics and, more recently, of the Milano-Cortina 2026 Games, it remains one of the most celebrated names in the Alps, blending world-class skiing, mountain culture and scenery that takes your breath away in every season.

In winter the area features large, modern lift-linked ski zones, steep technical slopes on the Tofane and Faloria, and quieter corners for ski touring and telemark away from the groomed runs. In summer, a network of trails and via ferrata opens up alpine ridgelines for hiking, climbing and E-bike tours. The town itself remains a cultural hub, with historic mountain huts, guided excursions and local mountain guides ready to craft tailor-made experiences for every level, from beginner to expert.
cortina.winterP1: Cortina d'Ampezzo is famous the world over for the Tofane and Faloria areas: steep technical pistes, scenic gondolas and classic long runs that helped write the history of alpine skiing. The dramatic Cinque Torri and the surrounding peaks offer superb skiing, former race tracks and iconic Dolomite panoramas, while the sunnier Faloria side suits riders looking for wide, well-groomed runs.
cortina.winterP2: Beyond the groomers, Cortina is an ideal gateway for ski mountaineering, snowshoeing and scenic winter hikes to some of the valley's most striking mountain huts. Evenings come alive with events, markets and historic bars, while those after a quieter pace find a warm, authentic atmosphere in the huts up in the mountains, well away from the buzz of the town centre.
cortina.summerP1: In summer Cortina becomes a reference point for rock climbing and high-altitude hiking: well-equipped via ferrata, exposed alpine ridgelines and panoramic cycle paths cross the Ampezzo valleys, with something for every level, from an easy family walk to the most demanding ferrata.
cortina.summerP2: Popular summer activities include guided hikes to historic rifugios, climbing the Dolomite walls that ring the town, and E-bike tours through valleys, forests and alpine meadows. There's also room to mix sport with culture, between small mountain museums, craft workshops and open-air evenings with a view of the Tofane.

sappada.title: Sappada
sappada.subtitle: Charming alpine village with family-friendly slopes and scenic singletracks
sappada.description:
Sappada is a charming alpine village known for its family-friendly slopes and scenic trails winding through forests and side valleys. Tucked into the north-eastern corner of Veneto, on the border with Friuli, it keeps a unique linguistic and cultural identity, that of the German-speaking Sappada minority, still felt today among the wooden chalets of the old centre.

The nearby valleys offer quiet singletracks and easy touring options for all levels, ideal for anyone taking their first steps in skiing or mountain biking. In winter you'll find gentle runs, a local snowpark and calm telemark lines; in summer the area opens up with mountain bike trails and walks through spruce forests, perfect for family days or more technical enduro rides higher up.
sappada.winterP1: Sappada offers approachable slopes and gentle, sun-facing terrain ideal for families and beginners. Easy backcountry routes and nearby huts make for straightforward first outings in ski touring and evening snowshoe walks, while the local snowpark is a good place to try your first jumps safely.
sappada.winterP2: Evenings in Sappada mean cozy lodges, wood-burning stoves and local Alpine culture, with traditional dishes that blend Venetian and Germanic influences: a quiet, genuine alternative to the larger, busier resorts, perfect for anyone after a slower, family-paced winter.
sappada.summerP1: Summer opens flowy forest trails and scenic alpine tracks around Sappada, laid out for relaxed all-day rides. The headwaters of the Piave river, which rises in these very valleys, make for a scenic starting point for riverside walks and nature trails suited to the whole family.
sappada.summerP2: Guided mountain bike tours, e-bike outings and scenic ridge hikes make Sappada a great base for low-key multi-day adventures, with a few technical stretches thrown in for anyone wanting a challenge. The huts higher up stay open through summer too, ready to welcome riders with a view over the Friulian Dolomites.

zoldoCivetta.title: Zoldo / Civetta
zoldoCivetta.subtitle: Wild ridgelines and secluded valleys, ideal for freeride and alpine adventures
zoldoCivetta.description:
The Zoldo valley and the Civetta massif offer an authentic Dolomite experience away from the busiest resorts and mass tourism. Known as the valley of the gelatieri, home to generations of Zoldano families who emigrated across Europe to open artisan ice-cream parlours, the area keeps a strong bond with the mountains and its traditions, between alpine huts, spruce forests and sheer walls brushing 3,000 metres.

In winter the area combines modern lift-served terrain in Civetta with quieter, steeper lines in Zoldo, ideal for telemark, ski mountaineering and freeride on snow that's often still untouched. Snow conditions and varied topography make it a great area for technical descents and touring. In summer you'll find high-altitude singletrack, forest descents and panoramic ridge trails that draw mountain bikers and hikers in for long rides and multi-day tours, with the north face of the Civetta, one of the most imposing in the Dolomites, always somewhere in view.
zoldoCivetta.winterP1: The Civetta ski area features long, well-groomed runs, steep couloirs and excellent freeride terrain, with enough vertical to satisfy even experienced skiers. Zoldo rounds out the area with quieter valleys, classic telemark lines and a strong mountain culture built on family-run huts, small historic lifts and an authentic relationship with the snow.
zoldoCivetta.winterP2: In Zoldo you can also arrange night outings: guided evening ski tours on skins and moonlit descents that turn familiar slopes into a magical alpine experience under the stars, far from the lights and noise of the bigger resorts. For anyone after quiet and a slower pace, this is one of the most genuine corners of the entire Belluno Dolomites.
zoldoCivetta.summerP1: Summer opens up a network of singletrack and high-altitude trails, from flowy routes through conifer forest to long alpine descents and the odd technical enduro section over roots and rock. Views of the Civetta's north face accompany much of the higher terrain, turning every climb into a visual reward as much as a physical one.
zoldoCivetta.summerP2: Mountain bike tours starting from Zoldo cross the Cadore valleys, panoramic ridgelines and wide meadows still dotted with working alpine huts: ideal for guided rides and multi-day tours, with stops at the huts for local cheese and cured meats before dropping back down.

cadore.title: Cadore
cadore.subtitle: The historic heart of the Dolomites, between the Tre Cime di Lavaredo and the lakes of Misurina and Centro Cadore
cadore.description:
Cadore is the historic cradle of the Belluno Dolomites, centred on Pieve di Cadore, birthplace of the painter Titian, as the area's cultural and symbolic hub. It's here, on Via Galghena, that the operating base for lessons and guided outings is set up, a convenient reference point for reaching the Tre Cime di Lavaredo, Lago di Misurina and the wide Lago di Centro Cadore basin in no time, all ringed by the Marmarole group and the Ampezzo Dolomites.

In winter the area offers family-friendly ski slopes and quick access to the larger Cortina and Auronzo resorts, plus a number of quieter ski touring routes; in summer, trails, via ferrata and mountain bike routes open up through forests, alpine lakes and historic mountain huts, across a territory that blends nature, art and the memory of the Great War.
cadore.winterP1: From Pieve di Cadore it's a short reach to the Auronzo ski area and the slopes facing the Tre Cime di Lavaredo, with ski touring and snowshoeing among some of the most photographed views in the Dolomites. The central location also makes it easy to head over to Cortina or Sappada for a day on bigger ski terrain, while still having a quiet base to return to each evening.
cadore.winterP2: Lago di Misurina, often frozen over in winter and ringed by conifers, and the area's small villages offer a quieter pace, ideal for riders looking for calmer slopes, walks in the fresh snow and evenings by the fire in a mountain hut, away from the buzz of the bigger ski centres.
cadore.summerP1: In summer Lago di Centro Cadore and Lago di Misurina become the starting point for scenic rides and lakeside walks, with the Marmarole and Tre Cime as a backdrop at every turn. The turquoise waters of Centro Cadore, fed by the Piave, also make a perfect stop for a refreshing break on longer tours.
cadore.summerP2: Trails, via ferrata and forest roads connect Pieve di Cadore to Auronzo and Misurina, perfect for guided mountain bike tours through history, art and nature. Along the way you'll pass historic mountain huts, traces of the Great War, and views over the Ampezzo Dolomites that turn every outing into a small journey through Cadore's mountain culture.

general.intro:
My name is Lorenzo Panzera, known to most simply as Panz. A few years ago I turned my passion for the mountains into a job: I'm a snowboard and telemark instructor and mountain bike guide, based in Pieve di Cadore, in the heart of the Belluno Dolomites.

The real job, though, is something else: showing you why I love these sports, and this mountain, so much, whether you're taking your first run or looking to sharpen your technique and style.

snowboard.description: Let's learn the basics of snowboarding together: carving, freestyle, freeride, snow tours, and whatever else you want to discover along the way.
snowboard.extendedDescription: snowboard is not just a sport but also a lifestyle, in fact my goal is not only to teach you the technique but also to make you experience all the emotions that this can give us! Whether you are a beginner or an expert, whether you want to improve your riding or freestyle technique, or whether you are interested in exploring the beautiful Dolomites, we will try together to create a path suitable for your needs to achieve your goals while having fun.

telemark.title: Telemark
telemark.description: Discover one of the oldest and most original skiing disciplines, fun is guaranteed.
telemark.extendedDescription: Telemark skiing combines the grace of nordic skiing with the thrill of alpine descents, creating a unique and rewarding experience on the slopes. As one of the oldest and most elegant skiing disciplines, telemark offers a distinctive free-heel technique that provides exceptional control and fluidity. I guide you through the fundamentals of telemark skiing, from proper stance and weight distribution to mastering those signature telemark turns. Whether you're completely new to the sport or looking to refine your technique, the stunning terrain of the Dolomites offers endless opportunities for telemark adventures.

mountainBike.title: Mountain Bike
mountainBike.description: Organized tours in the most spectacular locations in the Dolomites, basic techniques, enduro and bike park approach.
mountainBike.extendedDescription: Explore the Dolomites on two wheels with guided mountain bike tours and instruction tailored to your skill level. From scenic cross-country routes through alpine meadows to technical enduro trails and bike park sessions, I offer comprehensive guidance for mountain bikers of all abilities. Learn fundamental techniques including body positioning, braking, cornering, and climbing, or push your limits on challenging descents and jumps. The Dolomites provide some of the most spectacular and diverse mountain biking terrain in the world, with routes ranging from family-friendly paths to adrenaline-pumping downhill tracks.

description.p1: Outdoor sports, mountains, and nature: these are definitely the experiences that best define me. My name is Lorenzo Panzera, better known as Panz, and a few years ago I managed to turn my passions into a job, becoming a certified instructor of Snowboard, Telemark, and Mountain Bike Guide. This is where I want to start to tell you more about what I do and what I offer.
description.p2:
As snowboard instructor and telemark ski instructor, I want to bring as many people as possible closer to two disciplines that share not only snow but also the feeling of freedom, creativity, adrenaline, and fun! I will guide you step by step from the basics if you are beginners, or by perfecting technique and style together if you are more experienced.



As a mountain bike guide, a sport that is gaining more and more ground also thanks to E-bikes, I will take you to discover the most famous and spectacular places in the Dolomites, without neglecting less known but equally worthy trails and routes.
description.title3: Where do I carry out these activities?
description.p3:
Starting from my base, in Pieve di Cadore, I usually work in Cortina d’Ampezzo, a strategic location that, however, allows me to reach all the main locations of the Dolomites, depending on your needs.



Regardless of what you choose to do, my main goal will be to convey to you the same passion and love that I feel for these sports and for the mountains.
